नेपाल केरऽ पर्यटन राजधानी के रूप म॑ बहुत दिन स॑ पहचानलऽ जाय वाला पोखरा म॑ घरेलू आरू अंतर्राष्ट्रीय यात्री लेली प्रमुख गंतव्य के रूप म॑ प्रतिष्ठा के बावजूद महज एगो पांच सितारा होटल छै । बहुतो लोक ई मानैत छथि जे एहि शहर में हाई-एंड आगंतुक के पूरा करय वाला कईटा लग्जरी प्रॉपर्टी अछि, मुदा वास्तविकता एकदम अलग अछि. पोखरा मे एखन संचालित एकमात्र फाइव स्टार होटल पोखरा ग्रांड अछि ।

एकरऽ विपरीत भारत केरऽ सीमा स॑ सटलऽ जिला रूपन्देही विलासितापूर्ण आतिथ्य केरऽ असंभावित केंद्र के रूप म॑ उभरी क॑ सामने ऐलऽ छै । हालांकि एकरऽ स्थापित पर्यटन प्रोफाइल पोखरा के तरह नै छै, लेकिन जिला म॑ पहल॑ स॑ ही चारो फाइव स्टार होटल छै, जबकि सात आरू के निर्माणाधीन छै या फाइव स्टार मानक प॑ अपग्रेड करलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै ।

नेपाल केरऽ सीमावर्ती जिला म॑ उच्च श्रेणी के होटलऽ के तेजी स॑ बढ़ोत्तरी भारतीय आगंतुकऽ के बढ़तऽ संख्या, कैसिनो पर्यटन, धार्मिक पर्यटन, आरू सड़क संपर्क म॑ सुधार सहित कईएक कारकऽ के कारण बनलऽ छै । एकरऽ परिणाम ई छै कि दक्षिणी सीमा केरऽ शहर लग्जरी होटल निवेश केरऽ नया केंद्र के रूप म॑ तेजी स॑ उभर॑ लगलऽ छै ।

एक दशक पहिने नेपालक दक्षिणी सीमावर्ती शहर मुख्यतः सीमा पारक व्यापारक लेल जानल जाइत छल । आइ बहुतो में एकटा अलग तरहक परिवर्तन भ रहल अछि, कारण हाईवे के कात में, सीमा पार के आसपास, आ प्रमुख धार्मिक स्थल के पास लग्जरी होटल बढ़ि रहल अछि.

भैरहवा, नेपालगंज, धनगढी, महेन्द्रनगर, झापा, आ विराटनगर के पार पांच सितारा होटल, अंतर्राष्ट्रीय होटल ब्रांड आ कैसिनो रिसॉर्ट आतिथ्य परिदृश्य के नव रूप द रहल अछि. निवेशक न॑ ई क्षेत्र म॑ अरबों रुपया डाललकै, बढ़त॑ पर्यटकऽ के आगमन, धार्मिक पर्यटन, आरू भारतीय आगंतुकऽ के लगातार धारा प॑ दांव लगाय देल॑ छै ।

मुदा, चमकैत मुखौटाक पाछू एकटा बेसी जटिल यथार्थ अछि.

बहुतो लग्जरी होटल मे कमरा भरबा मे परेशानी भ रहल अछि। कईटा निवेशक एहि कारोबार स बाहर भ चुकल छथि, आओर दोसर कए बैंक क कर्ज चुकाबय मे दिक्कत भ रहल अछि। होटल संचालकऽ के कहना छै कि निवेश केरऽ उछाल मांग स॑ भी अधिक होय गेलऽ छै, आरू ई क्षेत्र लगातार पर्यटकऽ के आगमन के बजाय कैसिनो आरू सप्ताहांत म॑ आगंतुकऽ प॑ निर्भर होय गेलऽ छै ।

उद्योग जगत के नेता सिनी के तर्क छै कि ई निवेश के दीर्घकालिक सफलता बहुत हद तलक बेहतर अंतरराष्ट्रीय हवाई संपर्क प निर्भर करतै, खास करी क भैरहवा के गौतम बुद्ध अंतरराष्ट्रीय हवाई अड्डा प, साथ ही नेपालगंज आरू विराटनगर जैसनौ शहरौ स॑ बेहतर सीमा पार हवाई संपर्क प॑ भी निर्भर करतै ।

नेपाल के मैदान के किनारे लग्जरी होटल के उछाल 2015 के बाद तेजी सं बढ़ल.

सरकार केरऽ भैरहवा म॑ देश केरऽ दोसरऽ अंतर्राष्ट्रीय हवाई अड्डा बनाबै के फैसला, इलेक्ट्रॉनिक गेमिंग आरू मिनी कैसिनो केरऽ तेजी स॑ बढ़ोत्तरी, गंतव्य शादी केरऽ बढ़तऽ लोकप्रियता, आरू अप्रैल २०१६ स॑ लागू होय वाला बिहार म॑ शराब प॑ रोक स॑ निवेशकऽ क॑ उत्साहित करलऽ गेलै ।

ई सब विकास सब मिल क॑ सीमा के ठीक पार मनोरंजन, छोटऽ छुट्टी आरू शादी केरऽ जगह के तलाश करै वाला भारतीय आगंतुकऽ के मजबूत मांग पैदा करी देलकै ।

दू मास पहिने रुपन्देही आ कास्की के होटल मालिक के बीच बातचीत के दौरान होटल एसोसिएशन नेपाल पोखरा के अध्यक्ष लक्ष्मण सुबेदी नेपाल के लग्जरी हॉस्पिटैलिटी उद्योग के संतुलन कतेक नाटकीय रूप स बदलल अछि, इ बतौलनि।

ओ कहला जे पोखरा मे पैघ संख्या मे होटल अछि, मुदा एखन धरि मात्र एकटा फाइव स्टार प्रॉपर्टी अछि। "रूपन्देही मे पहिने सँ आधा दर्जन अछि।"

निवेशक गौतम बुद्ध अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय विमानस्थल आ बुद्धके जन्मस्थान लुम्बिनीमे अपन आशा जडलाके बाद रुपन्देही लग्जरी होटलके लेल नेपालके सबसँ तेजीसँ बढैत गन्तव्यके रुपमे उभरल अछि ।

लुम्बिनी हेरिटेज, सिद्धार्थ विलासा, टाइगर पैलेस बाय सोलटी, आ हयात पैलेस सहित पांच सितारा संपत्ति पहिने सं संचालित अछि.

भैरहवा-लुम्बिनी गलियारा क कात हयात रिजेंसी आ हॉलिडे इन क निर्माण भ रहल अछि, जखन कि लुम्बिनी पैलेस रिसॉर्ट कए मैरियट ब्रांडेड प्रॉपर्टी मे अपग्रेड कैल जा रहल अछि। तइयो भैरहवा मे एकटा आओर फाइव स्टार होटल क निर्माण भ रहल अछि।

अंतरराष्ट्रीय ब्रांड केरऽ आवागमन एक समय म॑ स्थानीय स्वामित्व वाला होटलऽ के बोलबाला वाला शहर लेली एगो महत्वपूर्ण बदलाव के रूप म॑ सामने ऐलऽ छै ।

लुम्बिनी हेरिटेज होटल के संचालक अनिल श्रेष्ठ कहलनि जे, अंतरराष्ट्रीय प्रबंधन कंपनी के आगमन स आतिथ्य के मानक बढ़ि रहल अछि। "एक के बाद एक क्वालिटी होटल खुलि रहल अछि, जाहि सं सेवा आओर सुविधा दुनू मे सुधार भ रहल अछि."

उद्यमी सब के कहना छै कि ई निवेश के बहुत हिस्सा गौतम बुद्ध अंतरराष्ट्रीय हवाई अड्डा के बौद्ध तीर्थयात्री आरू विदेशी पर्यटकौ के सेवा दै वाला एगो प्रमुख अंतर्राष्ट्रीय प्रवेश द्वार बनै के प्रत्याशा में करलौ गेलौ छेलै ।

पाल्पा के एक होटल में खड़ी भारतीय वाहन। पोस्ट फाइल फोटो

ओ अपेक्षा एखन धरि साकार नहि भेल अछि।

हालांकि ई हवाई अड्डा तीन साल स॑ भी अधिक समय स॑ संचालित छै, लेकिन नियमित रूप स॑ निर्धारित अंतर्राष्ट्रीय एयरलाइंस क॑ आकर्षित करै म॑ एकरा बहुत संघर्ष करना पड़लऽ छै । होटल मालिक एखनो ओहि आगंतुक क उछाल क इंतजार मे छथि जेकर ओ अनुमान लगा चुकल छलाह।

आब एहि जिला मे एक दर्जन स बेसी फोर स्टार होटल आ 100 स बेसी क्वालिटी होटल अछि। करीब एक दर्जन कैसिनो पहिने स संचालित अछि, जखन कि कईटा नव खुलल होटल गेमिंग सुविधा शुरू करबाक तैयारी मे अछि।

सिद्धार्थ होटल एसोसिएशन के अध्यक्ष सीपी श्रेष्ठ के अनुसार स्थानीय होटल के लेल कैसिनो कारोबार के प्रमुख स्रोत बनल अछि.

ओ कहला जे हमर सबहक अधिकांश आगंतुक भारतीय छथि जे मनोरंजन लेल अबैत छथि। "कैसिनो वाला स्टार होटल के संख्या बढ़ी रहलऽ छै । अगर गौतम बुद्ध अंतर्राष्ट्रीय हवाई अड्डा स॑ नियमित अंतरराष्ट्रीय उड़ान शुरू होय जाय छै त॑ निवेश आरू बढ़ी जैतै ।"

हुनकर अनुमान अछि जे असगर रूपन्देही क होटल उद्योग मे करीब 100 अरब टका क निवेश भ चुकल अछि।

तइयो रिटर्न उम्मीद स काफी कम भ गेल अछि। किछु निवेशक पर्याप्त मेहमान कए नहि आकर्षित करबा मे अपन होटल बेचि देलथि अछि, त किछु गोटे महत्वाकांक्षी परियोजना क वित्तपोषण लेल लेल गेल बैंक क कर्ज चुकाबय मे संघर्षरत छथि। होटल संचालक क कहब अछि जे नव संपत्ति मे निवेश जारी रहला क बावजूद कब्जा क दर अनुमान स कम अछि।

कैसिनो, गंतव्य विवाह, धार्मिक पर्यटन आ भारत सं छोट-छोट अवकाश यात्रा निवेश के मुख्य चालक बनि गेल अछि. एकरऽ बावजूद सीमा पट्टी केरऽ पार होटल संचालक ई बात क॑ स्वीकार करै छै कि कब्जा केरऽ दर उम्मीद स॑ कम छै, जेकरा स॑ कैसिनो आरू भोज राजस्व केरऽ महत्वपूर्ण स्रोत बनी गेलऽ छै ।

सुदुरपश्चिम प्रदेशमे धनगढी क्षेत्रके नवीनतम आतिथ्यकेन्द्रके रुपमे उभरल अछि ।

सबस पैघ परियोजना आईएचजी ग्रुप क तहत अंतरराष्ट्रीय ब्रांड हॉलिडे इन क साझेदारी मे चौलानी क्लब द्वारा बनाउल जा रहल पांच सितारा होटल अछि। 2.2 अरब टका क एहि होटल क अगिला साल खुलबाक अछि। एहि मे 115 कमरा होएत, जाहि मे पांचटा प्रीमियम सुइट सेहो शामिल अछि।

नेपाल केरऽ लग्जरी होटल केरऽ उछाल दक्षिणी सीमा के साथ खुली रहलऽ छै, पोखरा जैसनऽ पारंपरिक गंतव्यऽ म॑ नै, जेकरा म॑ अखनी भी केवल एक फाइव स्टार होटल छै ।

चौलानी क्लब के प्रबंध निदेशक मान सिंह साउद के कहनाय छनि जे एहि परियोजना सं ओहि प्रांत मे अंतरराष्ट्रीय स्तर के आतिथ्य आओत, जाहि मे बहुत दिन सं लग्जरी आवास के कमी अछि.

ओ कहला जे एहि होटल स सुदुरपस्चिम मे पर्यटन आ निवेश कए ऊंचाई भेटत आ प्रांत मे आतिथ्य क नव मानक तय होएत।

एकटा आओर पैघ परियोजना चारि सितारा सनलाइट होटल सेहो धनगढी मे पूरा होबय बला अछि. ई परियोजना शहर केरऽ दीर्घकालिक पर्यटन क्षमता प॑ निवेशकऽ के बढ़तऽ विश्वास के एगो आरू संकेत छै ।

ओहि आशावाद केरऽ बहुत हिस्सा पड़ोसी देश भारत स॑ बढ़तऽ सीमा पार स॑ आवागमन आरू ई उम्मीद प॑ आधारित छै कि पश्चिमी नेपाल आबै वाला सालऽ म॑ अधिक व्यापारिक यात्री, घरेलू पर्यटक आरू अंतर्राष्ट्रीय आगंतुक क॑ आकर्षित करतै ।

सुदूर पश्चिम क शहर महेन्द्रनगर पहिने स कैसिनो क गंतव्य बनि चुकल अछि।

आब एहि शहर में गेमिंग सुविधा वाला तीन सितारा होटल संचालित अछि, जाहि में ओपेरा होटल सब सं पुरान आ नीक सं स्थापित अछि. लगभग दू दशक स॑ संचालित ई होटल हाल ही म॑ फोर स्टार के दर्जा म॑ अपग्रेड होय गेलऽ छै आरू अपनऽ कैसिनो परिचालन क॑ सीएमजी क्लब क॑ पट्टा प॑ द॑ देल॑ छै ।

होटल प्रबंधक गणेश चटौत कहला जे भारतीय आगंतुक ग्राहक आधार पर हावी रहैत अछि।

ओ कहला जे भारतीय पर्यटक हमर मुख्य ग्राहक छथि। "मुदा पर्यटन गतिविधि धीमा भेला स कारोबार आओर कठिन भ गेल अछि।"

डायमंड होटल आ रूपम होटल हालक वर्ष मे खुजल अछि। डायमंड पहिने सं कैसिनो संचालित करैत अछि, जखन कि रूपम अपन गेमिंग संचालन लीज पर द देने अछि.

हीरा क मालिक सुरेंद्र सिंह कहला जे होटल कए 50 करोड़ स बेसी क लागत स फोर स्टार प्रॉपर्टी मे अपग्रेड कैल जा रहल अछि।

ओ कहला जे हमरा सब कए उम्मीद अछि जे एक साल क भीतर इ परियोजना पूरा भ जाएत।

हालांकि होटल निर्माण जारी अछि, मुदा कैसिनो एहि संपत्तिक मुख्य आकर्षण बनल अछि.

सिंह के अनुसार कैसिनो के उपयोग करै लेली रोजाना 150 स॑ 200 के बीच आगंतुक आबै छै, जेकरा म॑ स॑ बहुत लोग नई दिल्ली तलक के भारतीय शहरऽ स॑ आबै छै ।

आगू पूर्व बाँके मे नेपालगंज एकटा आओर उदाहरण प्रस्तुत करैत अछि जे कोना कैसिनो पर्यटन स्थानीय आतिथ्य उद्योगक रीढ़ बनि गेल अछि ।

मुदा, सीमावर्ती अन्य अनेक शहरक विपरीत नेपालगंजक होटलमें आगंतुक लोकनिक व्यापक मिश्रण भेटत. भारतीय पर्यटक जुआ खेलय अबैत छथि, जखन कि घरेलू यात्री एहि शहर के व्यावसायिक केंद्र के रूप में उपयोग करैत छथि.

ई शहर हुमला मार्ग स॑ तिब्बत केरऽ कैलाश मनसरोवर जाय वाला तीर्थयात्री लेली प्रवेश द्वार के रूप म॑ भी काम करै छै ।

होटल एहि व्यापक मांग कए पूरा करबा लेल विविधता अनलक अछि, कैसिनो क संग-संग स्पा, सम्मेलन सुविधा आ भोज हॉल मे निवेश केलक अछि ।

होटल सोलटी वेस्टेंड प्रीमियर क सेल्स मैनेजर प्रतीक श्रेष्ठ कहला जे आब कारोबार केवल गेमिंग तक सीमित नहि अछि।

ओ कहला जे हम कॉरपोरेट कार्यक्रम, सम्मेलन, विवाह आ संगठनात्मक आयोजन क आयोजन करैत छी। "विदेशी ट्रेकर्स सेहो भारतीय आगंतुकक संग एतय रहैत छथि."

फोर स्टार संपत्ति लॉर्ड्स प्लाजा स्थित डायमंड पैलेस कैसिनो आ स्पा सुविधा क आसपास अपना कए ठाढ़ क लेने अछि ।

होटल केरऽ सेल्स मैनेजर भोजराज शाह न॑ कहलकै कि ९५ कमरा म॑ नियमित रूप स॑ भारतीय मेहमान बैठै छै, जेकरा म॑ स॑ बहुत सारा कमरा खास करी क॑ कैसिनो लेली पास के सीमा पार करी क॑ पार करै छै ।

पौवा ब्रांड के तहत पांच सितारा होटल के निर्माण सेहो चलि रहल अछि, जे बाजार के चुनौतीपूर्ण स्थिति के बावजूद निवेशक के लगातार आत्मविश्वास के संकेत दैत अछि.

गेमिंग, गंतव्य विवाह, धार्मिक पर्यटन आ भारत सं सप्ताहांत में आबय वाला लोक बहुत रास हाईएंड होटल के आमदनी के प्राथमिक स्रोत बनि गेल अछि.

सिद्धार्थ बिजनेस ग्रुप आफ हॉस्पिटैलिटी के क्षेत्रीय कार्यकारी निदेशक केशव न्यौपाने कहलनि जे, नेपालगंज के सामरिक स्थान के कारण एकरा सीमावर्ती अन्य बहुत रास शहर के मुकाबले व्यापक पर्यटन आधार भेटैत अछि।

कैसिनो आबै वाला के अलावा भारतीय तीर्थयात्री कैलाश मनसरोवर के रास्ता में नेपालगंज के रास्ता स॑ यात्रा करै छै, जबकि दोसरऽ लोग लुम्बिनी आरू पशुपतिनाथ के दौरा के संयोजन करै छै ।

होटल उद्यमी संघ केरऽ बांके जिला अध्याय के अध्यक्ष भीमलाल कंडेल न॑ कहलकै कि पूरा जिला म॑ होटलऽ म॑ लगभग १२ अरब रुपया के निवेश करलऽ गेलऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ अब॑ लगभग ३,००० छोटऽ आरू बड़ऽ आवास के सुविधा छै ।

दक्षिण मध्य नेपालमे पूर्वी नवलपरासीके त्रिवेणी क्षेत्रमे सेहो आतिथ्य निवेशमे उछाल देखल गेल अछि ।

भारतीय पर्यटक आ तीर्थयात्री के भोजन देबय वाला होटल आओर रेस्टोरेंट मे एक अरब रुपया सं बेसि के निवेश भ चुकल अछि.

ग्रांड त्रिवेणी रिसॉर्ट के परिचालन शुरू भ गेल अछि आओर कैसिनो सेवा शुरू करय के तैयारी मे अछि. एकरऽ मालिक सुशील कुमार बनिया न॑ कहलकै कि ई परियोजना विशेष रूप स॑ भारतीय पर्यटकऽ के साथ-साथ धार्मिक रूप स॑ महत्वपूर्ण त्रिवेणी क्षेत्र म॑ आबै वाला तीर्थयात्री सिनी क॑ लक्षित करै छै ।

एकटा आओर परियोजना तिरुपति रिज़ॉर्ट एंड कैसिनो सेहो परिचालन शुरू करबाक तैयारी मे अछि।

होटल उद्यमी संघ केरऽ नवलपुर जिला अध्याय के अध्यक्ष संतोष राणा न॑ कहलकै कि हाल के सालऽ म॑ जिला म॑ एक अरब रुपया स॑ भी अधिक के ताजा निवेश के प्रवाह होय गेलऽ छै, कैन्हेंकि उद्यमी सीमा पार स॑ पर्यटन के पूंजी बनाबै के कोशिश करी रहलऽ छै ।

निवेश के लहर नेपाल के पूर्वी सीमावर्ती जिला में सेहो पसरल अछि, जाहि में झापा आ मोरंग तेजी सं नव आतिथ्य केंद्र के रूप में उभरल अछि, जेकरा कैसिनो आ भारतीय पर्यटक यातायात सं ईंधन भेटल अछि.

मेचीनगर केरऽ पांच सितारा डीलक्स होटल मेची क्राउन आठ बीघा (५.४ हेक्टेयर) म॑ फैललऽ छै आरू एकरा म॑ १०५ कमरा, विला, रेस्टोरेंट, बैंक्वेट हॉल, हेलीपैड, स्पा, स्विमिंग पूल, जिमनैजियम, आरू अन्य खेल सुविधा उपलब्ध छै ।

एकरऽ मालिक बलराम सापकोटा न॑ कहलकै कि पूर्वी नेपाल म॑ गुणवत्तापूर्ण आवास केरऽ बहुत दिन स॑ कमी ​​रहला स॑ हुनी ई निवेश करलकै । हुनी आरू कहलकै कि हुनकऽ कैसिनो वेगास म॑ रोज भारी संख्या म॑ भारतीय आगंतुक आबै छै ।

एकटा आओर पांच सितारा संपत्ति होटल अश्वत्था पिछला साल मेचिनगर मे मीडिया उद्यमी प्रज्जवल घिमिरे क 1.3 अरब टका क निवेश स खुलल छल।

बिर्तमोद मे किंग्सबरी होटल सेहो खुलल अछि, जाहि स झापा मे पांच सितारा होटल क संख्या तीन भ गेल अछि।

निवेश बढ़ैत रहैत अछि।

होटल ईस्टर्न नेपाल प्राइवेट लिमिटेड करीब ९३४ मिलियन रुपैया के निवेश स धुलाबारी मे एकटा आओर फाइव स्टार होटल बना रहल अछि, जखन कि बिर्तमोद मे एकटा आओर लग्जरी प्रॉपर्टी पूरा होबय बला अछि।

पड़ोसी विराटनगर मे हालहि मे भारतीय आतिथ्य समूह क शहर मे पहिल होटल आ नेपाल मे ओकर तेसर संपत्ति क रूप मे लेमन ट्री प्रीमियम व्यावसायिक संचालन शुरू केलक अछि।

स्थानीय उद्यमी मनोज बिक्रम शाह, कबिन श्रेष्ठ, विकास चौधरी आ प्रशांत टेटेड क करीब दू अरब टका क निवेश स बनल एहि होटल मे डीलक्स आवास स ल कए प्रेसिडेंट सुइट तक क 80 कमरा अछि।

होटल संचालक के कहनाय छनि जे पूर्वी नेपाल मे बांग्लादेशी पर्यटक सेहो रहय लागल छथिन्ह, जाहि सं भारतीय आगंतुक के संग संग मांग के एकटा आओर स्रोत बढ़ि गेल अछि.

नेपालक सबसँ व्यस्त स्थल सीमा पार आ अपन सबसँ पैघ वाणिज्यिक केन्द्र मे सँ एक रहितो वीरगंज लग्जरी होटल उछाल मे अपवाद बनल अछि ।

शहर मे एखनो कोनो फाइव स्टार होटल नहि अछि।

एकर बदला मे तीनटा फोर स्टार प्रॉपर्टी-क्लार्क्स रिज़ॉर्ट, सिद्धार्थ दियालो आ सरोवर- बाजार मे हावी अछि।

शहर केरऽ सबस॑ पुरानऽ प्रतिष्ठानऽ म॑ स॑ एक बिश्वो होटल तीन सितारा संपत्ति के रूप म॑ काम जारी छै, जबकि मकालू, पूजन आरू सूरज जैसनऽ होटल न॑ अपनऽ सुविधा क॑ अपग्रेड करी क॑ प्रतिस्पर्धी बनलऽ रहै छै ।

एखन क्लार्क रिज़ॉर्ट, सिद्धार्थ दियालो, सरोवर, बिश्वो होटल आ होटल सूरज स पांच मिनी कैसिनो संचालित अछि।

हालांकि वीरगंज देश केरऽ सबसें बड़ऽ मात्रा म॑ सीमा पार स॑ व्यापार संभाल॑ छै आरू देश केरऽ सबसें बड़ऽ व्यापारिक समुदाय म॑ स॑ एक छै, लेकिन एकरऽ आतिथ्य क्षेत्र अभी तलक अन्य सीमावर्ती शहरऽ म॑ देखलऽ जाय वाला निवेश केरऽ पैमाना क॑ आकर्षित नै कर॑ सकलऽ छै ।

full_article:
Kathmandu. The number of Rohingya refugees in Nepal has reached 526, the police have stated. Speaking at a press conference at the Police Headquarters on Friday, Police Spokesperson (DIG) Abinarayan Kafle said that the number of Rohingya refugees has increased. He said, 'The number of Rohingyas has now reached 526.'

Among the Rohingyas staying in Lasuntar of Kapan and Lalitpur, 162 are men. DIG Kafle stated that Rohingyas have been residing in the Sunakothi area of Lalitpur. The Rohingya Muslim community, who came to Nepal from Myanmar via Bangladesh, had been living in a camp in Lasuntar for a long time. There is also a Rohingya camp at Ram Mandir in Kapan.

title: Nepal Police Identifies Social Media Misuse and Financial Crimes as Key Security Challenges - Ratopati
description: Nepal Police Identifies Social Media Misuse and Financial Crimes as Key Security Challenges  Ratopati
publisher.title: Ratopati
full_article: Kathmandu. Nepal Police has identified the misuse of social media and increasing financial crimes as the main security challenges at present. Speaking at a press conference on Friday, Deputy Inspector General and spokesperson Binod Singh KC stated that there is an increased risk of communal, ethnic, and religious harmony being disturbed due to misinformation and disinformation disseminated through social media. Police statistics show a significant rise in financial crimes and cybercrimes in recent times. Spokesperson KC informed that among the analysis of ten major types of crimes, 'scamming' related to cybercrime has been observed more frequently. 'Recent incidents have confirmed that any activity, if not coordinated and prevented in time, can take a dire form,' said spokesperson KC, adding, 'We have taken the security challenges created by the misuse of social media seriously.' He stated that to overcome such security challenges and minimize potential crimes, the Nepal Police Headquarters has formulated a special action plan and initiated its implementation. He mentioned that the police administration is alert from the beginning for crime prevention and will proceed according to the action plan. Nepal Police has put forward a plan to modernize the organization and make it technology-friendly by making extensive improvements in information technology, human resource management, and physical infrastructure. At the press conference held on Friday, DIG KC provided detailed information about the future form and action plan of the police. The police have proposed to establish an 'Anti Cyber Scam Center' to reduce cybercrime and scamming incidents. This center, to be located at the Cyber Bureau, will have representatives from Nepal Police, Nepal Rastra Bank, Bankers Association, Nepal Telecommunications Authority, and Internet Service Providers as contact persons. DIG KC stated that considering the increasing cybercrime, the Inspector General of Police has given high priority to this project. In terms of physical infrastructure, the police aim to establish an 'Integrated Command Center' at all three levels – central, provincial, and district. This will facilitate coordination among representatives of all concerned bodies in emergency situations. Similarly, to make traffic management modern and service-oriented, GPS systems will be installed in all patrol teams and vehicles. To address communal and security challenges that may arise through misinformation, disinformation, and 'deepfakes', there is a plan to expand the Social Media Coordination Desk to the provincial level. The police have stated that such activities will be identified and discouraged in time through the use of artificial intelligence. To make crime investigation more objective, 'Cyber Desks' will be established in all district police offices. Furthermore, the Forensic Science Laboratory and Digital Forensic Lab will be expanded to the provincial level, and skilled manpower will be deployed. The police have also initiated the process of purchasing advanced equipment such as Facial Recognition System, Call Interception, Blockchain Analysis Tools, and Crime Scene Scanners. Regarding human resource management, a policy is being prepared to implement online training, leadership development, and performance-based evaluation systems, informed KC. Necessary actions are also being taken based on the report of the study committee formed for police uniform modification. Information was given that the work on the National Police Training Institute being constructed in Panauti, Kavre, with the grant assistance of the Government of India, is 91 percent complete. Out of approximately 822 ropanis of land, 646 ropanis are covered by this project, under which 48 buildings and a total of 67 structures are being constructed. Police have also prioritized the upgrade of the radio communication system and the expansion of an integrated smart CCTV network at urban entry points, informed KC.

Kathmandu, Aug 7: More than 500 Rohingya refugees have illegally entered Nepal due to the open border and lack of technology-based security surveillance.

Spokesperson of Nepal Police Headquarter, Abinarayan Kafle, shared that such number of Rohingya people have entered Nepal via the Nepal-India border in different periods.

According to police, there are 526 Rohingya people-- 162 male, 148 female and 216 children - in Nepal. They have been found residing in Kapan, Lasuntar and Ram Mandir in Kathmandu and Sunakothi area in Lalitpur.

Kafle mentioned that security personnel deputed at border areas have been directed to stop such persons entering Nepal.

At a news conference organised at the Police Headquarters today, he opined, "Problem has surfaced to identify Rohingya refugees due to similar appearance to Nepalis and due to open border and lack of technology-based security surveillance."

Special surveillance has been increased to stop illegal entry of foreign nationals, he argued.

The police Spokesperson mentioned that police personnel have been kept on high-alert to minimize possible losses from natural disaster, adding around 10,000 police personnel have been kept on standby for disaster preparedness and its response.

He clarified that activities are underway in coordination with bodies concerned to resume services affected due to disaster as soon as possible.(RSS)

Key Takeaways:

57 deaths, 757 incidents across 64 districts since April 14

80% of fatalities linked to delayed treatment, reliance on faith healers

Madhes Province worst-hit: 122 cases, 21 deaths; Lumbini 16 deaths

Officials warn of kraits' nocturnal bites and limited antivenom supplies

Delays in reaching medical facilities are turning snakebites into a deadly monsoon hazard in Nepal, with 57 people killed in 757 incidents across 64 districts since April 14, according to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA).

Related Articles Kathmandu Valley reports highest injuries; Lumbini records most deaths Three dead, 21 injured in 42 disaster incidents across Nepal in 24 hours

Health officials say about 80 per cent of snakebite deaths occur because victims take too long to reach treatment centres, with reliance on faith healers, traditional remedies and home treatments continuing to pose major risks, particularly in rural and Tarai communities.

Snakebite incidents typically rise during the monsoon as floods and heavy rain force snakes out of their habitats and into human settlements.

Dr Amrit Pokharel, chief of the Epidemiology Management Section at the Epidemiology and Disease Control Division, said farmers, children and women are among those most exposed. He warned against practices such as tying cords around bites, attempting to suck out venom or seeking traditional treatment.

Pokharel also highlighted the danger posed by kraits, which often bite people while they are sleeping. Such bites may cause little pain and leave no visible mark, meaning victims may not realise they have been bitten until the venom spreads.

57 deaths since April

According to NDRRMA undersecretary Ram Bahadur KC, between April 14 and August 4 Nepal recorded 57 deaths and 709 injuries from snakebites. Longer-term data show 1,678 incidents and 301 deaths between 2016 and 2026, with a fatality rate of 17.93 per cent.

Since April, Madhes Province has been hardest hit, recording 122 incidents and 21 deaths. Lumbini reported 16 deaths, followed by Koshi with nine, Sudurpaschim with seven, Karnali with three and Bagmati with one.

Officials say treatment is complicated by limited antivenom supplies, dependence on imports and inadequate intensive-care facilities. The government has identified Kanchanpur, Kailali and Palpa as priority districts for antivenom distribution.

Children face higher fatality risks than adults, prompting calls for greater protection and awareness.

Nepal is home to several venomous species, including cobras, kraits and Russell's vipers. Health authorities advise using torches at night, wearing boots and long clothing in fields, clearing vegetation around homes, controlling rodents and avoiding sleeping directly on the floor.

Officials have also called for snakebite preparedness and awareness campaigns before and during the monsoon, warning that climate change-linked rainfall patterns could further increase human-snake encounters.

बच्चाक कें वयस्कक कें अपेक्षा जानलेवा कें अधिक जोखिम कें सामना करएय पड़एयत छै, जे बेसि सुरक्षा आ जागरूकता कें आह्वान करएयत छै.

नेपालमे कोबरा, क्राइट आ रसेल वाइपर सहित अनेक जहरीला प्रजातिक निवास अछि । स्वास्थ्य अधिकारियक कें सलाह छै कि रात मे मशाल कें उपयोग करनाय, खेत मे बूट आ लंबा कपड़ा पहननाय, घरक कें आसपास वनस्पति साफ करनाय, कृंतक कें नियंत्रित करनाय आ सीधा फर्श पर सुतय सं बचनाय.

अधिकारी न॑ मानसून स॑ पहल॑ आरू मानसून के दौरान साँप के काटै के तैयारी आरू जागरूकता अभियान के आह्वान भी करल॑ छै, जेकरा म॑ चेतावनी देलऽ गेलऽ छै कि जलवायु परिवर्तन स॑ जुड़लऽ बारिश के पैटर्न स॑ मानव-सांप के मुठभेड़ म॑ आरू वृद्धि होय सकै छै ।

title: Nepal’s co-op fraud victims stage protests in Kathmandu - Co-operative News
description: Nepal’s co-op fraud victims stage protests in Kathmandu  Co-operative News
publisher.title: Co-operative News
full_article:
Victims of the Nepalese finance co-op fraud have staged fresh demonstrations in Kathmandu to demand the immediate return of their deposits.

The rally, under the banner under the banner of the National Campaign for Cooperative Depositors Protection, also calls for a reliable plan to secure their funds, reports Nepal News.

Protesters marched to the office of the Problematic Cooperative Management Committee (PCMC) in Buddhanagar, and onward to the National Cooperative Regulatory Authority in Pulchowk.

They carried copies of previous agreements signed with the government, and voiced frustration that ministers are discriminating between small and large depositors in the refund process.

The protests are the latest turn in a corruption scandal that has rocked the country’s finance co-op sector over the past few years, with embezzlement of member’s funds on a massive scale.

Hundreds of arrests have been made and concerns raised over regulatory oversight and political influence.

In May, it was reported that the government has started returning deposits to small savers, with the PCMC stating initial priority was going to depositors with smaller savings. It added that refunds will be processed gradually based on classification of deposit amounts.

Related: Fallout continues from Nepal’s co-op scandal

Around 76,000 depositors of troubled co-operatives are owed approximately Rs46bn (£224m, US$300m) in total, say officials.

Most of these are small depositors, with less than Rs500,000; those with more than Rs500,000 are classified as large depositors.

Out of the total, around 18,000 people fall under the large depositor category.

The PCMC is focusing on institutions formally declared troubled, but the Kathmandu Post reports that victims and experts warn this excludes a much bigger number of co-ops that have collapsed, whose operators have disappeared and whose members have been protesting for years with no clear path to recovering their savings.

The federal government has so far declared 23 co-ops troubled, while Bagmati Province has listed five and Koshi Province one.

But victims’ representatives say that more than 500 institutions across the country have stopped returning deposits even though they have not been officially classified as problematic – and victims fall outside the government’s refund programme.

title: What Indian mountaineers feel about Nepal’s likely move to make permission for Everest climb tougher - The Federal
description: What Indian mountaineers feel about Nepal’s likely move to make permission for Everest climb tougher  The Federal
publisher.title: The Federal
full_article:
For generations of mountaineers, Everest represented the culmination of a lifelong ambition. It was the prize after years of preparation and countless hours spent on smaller peaks. Today, it is also a booming tourism industry, a social media milestone and, for some, a goal that money can fast-track.

Now, Nepal is reportedly considering a significant change to who gets the opportunity to scale it. According to news reports, under a proposal included in its new draft Tourism Bill, anyone seeking an Everest permit would first have to successfully climb a peak above 7,000 metres and that qualifying ascent would have to be completed in Nepal itself. The proposal has found broad support among Indian mountaineers who believe climbing Everest should demand prior experience. "For Indian mountaineers, I feel they should attempt at least four or five peaks between 6,500 and 7,500 metres before Everest," says Colonel Vijay Singh, president of the Indian Mountaineering Foundation. "India has thousands of technically difficult peaks." While the Colonel did not comment on the purported proposal to make the qualifying ascent mandatory in Nepal, other Indian mountaineers question why experience gained on equally demanding mountains outside Nepal should not count. “Everest is still the pinnacle of mountaineering. The mountain demands respect and preparation,” says Dr Anshu Jamsenpa, the Padma Shri awardee from Arunachal Pradesh who has summited Everest five times, including a world-record double ascent within five days in 2017. Jamsenpa supports the principle behind the proposal. Everest, she says, should never be treated as a commercial tourist destination. “Experience teaches lessons that cannot be learnt on Everest itself,” she says. The proposed qualification rule is one of several changes Nepal is considering as it attempts to address concerns surrounding safety, medical fitness, insurance, expedition management and environmental damage on the world’s highest mountain. Last year, Nepal rolled out a five-year ‘Everest Cleaning Action Plan’ to keep the world’s highest peak from turning into a “dumping ground”. As per reports, a cleaning campaign in 2019 had seen the collection of 10,800 kgs of biodegradable and non-biodegradable waste from Everest. Now, the purported proposal to tighten permission norms follows a record spring climbing season (late March to early May). Nepal reportedly issued 492 Everest permits during this period, while 1,008 successful ascents were recorded from its side of the mountain, including guides and repeat summits. However, the season also saw the death of five climbers, including two Indians. For Jamsenpa, better preparation would make Everest safer for everyone involved. But she does not believe Nepal should be the only place where that preparation can take place. If the proposed rule becomes law, she believes the Indian Mountaineering Foundation should take up the issue with Nepal and seek recognition for qualifying climbs completed in India. “Indian climbers should be able to train on our own mountains and have that experience recognised,” she says. That combination, support for compulsory experience, but opposition to the Nepal-only condition, was echoed by several Indian mountaineers. Also read: Why online trolling of Gen Z women dissenters is yet another proof of growing digital misogyny Captain Ram Bahadur Mall has climbed Everest from both sides. The Army officer reached the summit through Tibet in 2007 and scaled the peak again via Nepal’s South Col route in 2013. He has climbed nearly 30 Himalayan peaks, including Makalu, and has served as an instructor at the National Institute of Mountaineering and Adventure Sports in Arunachal Pradesh. “Technically, Everest is not the hardest mountain,” Mall says. “The altitude, the duration and the environment make it formidable.” Modern expeditions may have reduced some of the logistical challenges through fixed ropes and organised support, he says, but none of that can replace a climber’s understanding of their own body. “Climbing another high mountain first teaches you to become self-reliant,” he says. “You learn how to manage yourself and your body before attempting Everest.” Mall therefore agrees that previous high-altitude experience should be mandatory. What he disputes is the attempt to define valid experience through a national boundary. “Experience should be mandatory, but why only Nepal?” he asks. India has peaks capable of exposing climbers to comparable altitude, weather, isolation and expedition conditions, he says. A documented ascent in the Indian Himalayas should not become irrelevant simply because it was made on the other side of Nepal’s border, he believes. Nepal reportedly issued 492 Everest permits during this spring, while 1,008 successful ascents were recorded from its side of the mountain. However, the season also saw the death of five climbers, including two Indians. Photo: iStock

For Chandrakant “Ricky”, a Himachal Pradesh-based mountaineer who has worked alongside State Disaster Response Force teams during rescue and recovery operations, judgement is the real value of previous experience.

“People think Everest is mainly about physical fitness. At that altitude, it becomes more mental than physical,” he says. Ricky says climbers learn to understand fatigue and the importance of turning back only through longer expeditions, not during a brief training programme. “Experience is the biggest safety net.” He supports a gradual progression towards Everest. As the others, however, he too feels the debate should remain focused on preparedness rather than geography. That concern becomes sharper when the problem is viewed through the changing culture around Everest. Prakriti Varshney, who summited Everest in 2022, is an adventure athlete and one of India’s most visible mountaineering voices on social media. She has seen how online attention has altered the way Everest is imagined. “Many people have a bucket-list dream but no blueprint,” she says. Varshney is firmly in favour of a prior 7,000-metre ascent. Fewer people on the route, she believes, would make the mountain safer for climbers who have spent years preparing for it and would also reduce the burden on an already strained environment. When she climbed Everest, she recalls around 390 to 400 permit-holding climbers being on the mountain during the season. The latest figures are significantly higher. “Less crowd would make Everest safer for serious climbers,” she says. “The human waste is also becoming a major issue,” she adds, highlighting the other concern about increasing Everest footfall. Varshney believes social media has fundamentally changed Everest’s image. High-profile mountaineering projects, including those of Nirmal Purja (the Nepali-British mountaineer who was killed last month when an avalanche struck Broad Peak in the Karakoram range while he was attempting to summit it), gave Himalayan climbing unprecedented visibility and inspired many more people to dream of the mountain. But they also fuelled an obsession with records and online attention. “Everest has become about records,” she says. Varshney is herself a storyteller with a large online following, but says there are moments when recording has to stop. “I wouldn’t put my life and others at risk to create content,” she says. She has seen others continue filming in situations where their attention should have been entirely on the mountain. More seriously, she has encountered climbers who appeared physically or mentally unprepared for the conditions. She recalls one young Indian climber who, she believed, had been pushed towards the attempt by her family despite not being ready, struggling to breathe and requiring help from others. “Everyone around comes at risk because of them,” she says. “If something goes wrong, it is often the Sherpas (members of a Himalayan clan known for their mountaineering skills who often accompany expeditions) who pay the price.” That is one reason she supports a filtering mechanism before Everest. Commercial agencies have already built a large business around the mountain, she says. Some operators in India also market the climb aggressively because the financial rewards are considerable. “It has become a big money affair,” she adds. If a 7,000-metre summit in Nepal becomes compulsory, the qualifying expedition itself could soon become part of that same commercial pipeline. That possibility gives the proposal an economic dimension for India. Also read: Why for Modi govt, struggling to make sense of Gen Z protest playbook, abusive videos are least of worries Tsering Wange, founder of Himalayan Holidays and president of the North East India Tourism Confederation, supports stronger safety rules. But he believes the Nepal-only condition could divert both climbers and revenue away from the Indian Himalayas. “India has mountains that prepare climbers just as well,” he says. One of the concerns in recent years has been the increasing waste dump on the world's highest peak. Photo: iStock

An aspiring Everest climber may already spend years training on Indian peaks, employing Indian guides and using local expedition services. Under the [purported] proposed rule, that experience would not be enough.

“If qualifying climbs are restricted to Nepal, naturally the tourism benefits stay there,” Wange says. The rule could therefore strengthen Nepal’s already well-developed mountaineering economy while weakening incentives to organise preparatory expeditions in India. Climbers who might otherwise train on Indian Himalayan peaks could decide that it makes more financial and practical sense to complete the entire progression in Nepal. While Wange said it was difficult to put an exact value on India's Himalayan mountaineering economy, he described it as a multi-billion-dollar industry that supports hundreds of trekking and mountaineering clubs across the country. He estimates that 15–20 per cent of that business could shift to Nepal if the reported qualifier is put in place. A compulsory 7000-metre preparatory summit in Nepal is also likely to pinch aspiring climbers. While mountaineers The Federal spoke to did not bring up the subject, reports suggest such a criterion for permission to climb Everest is like to up expedition costs of Indian mountaineers by a few lakhs. For Wange, the answer is for India to make a stronger case for the recognition of comparable Indian climbs. He believes the Government of India and the Indian Mountaineering Foundation should engage with Nepal, particularly on behalf of Indian climbers. At the same time, he says, the debate should force India to look at its own shortcomings. “This should encourage India to invest more seriously in mountaineering,” Wange says. A negotiated arrangement recognising approved Indian peaks could protect the safety principle behind Nepal’s proposal without making geography the sole measure of valid experience. Veteran mountaineer Kamal Sharma, who has been active in the Himalayas since the 1990s, believes the debate also reflects how rapidly the culture of climbing has changed. “Earlier, climbing was the reward for years of preparation,” he says. “Today, there is much more pressure to reach the summit and show it.” Sharma supports a prerequisite before Everest but, like the others, does not believe that experience should count only when it is gained in Nepal. “If someone has climbed a comparable peak elsewhere and can prove it, that should also count,” he says. Across conversations with Indian mountaineers, there was broad agreement on one point: Everest should demand genuine high-altitude experience. The disagreement begins only when geography enters the discussion.

ओ कहैत छथि जे लोक कए लगैत अछि जे एवरेस्ट मुख्य रूप स शारीरिक फिटनेस क बारे मे अछि, ओहि ऊंचाई पर इ शारीरिक स बेसी मानसिक भ जाइत अछि। रिकी के कहना छै कि पर्वतारोही थकान आरू पीछे मुड़ै के महत्व क॑ समझना सीखै छै केवल लम्बा अभियान के माध्यम स॑, नै कि संक्षिप्त प्रशिक्षण कार्यक्रम के दौरान । “अनुभव सबसँ पैघ सुरक्षा जाल अछि।” ओ एवरेस्ट दिस क्रमिक प्रगति के समर्थन करैत छथि । मुदा, आन लोक जकाँ हुनका सेहो आयल अछि. ओ कहैत छथि जे बहुत लोक कए बकेट लिस्ट क सपना रहैत अछि मुदा कोनो खाका नहि। वार्शनी पहिने 7000 मीटर क चढ़ाई क दृढ़ता स पक्ष मे छथि। हुनकऽ मानना ​​छै कि ई मार्ग प॑ कम लोगऽ के कमी स॑ ई पहाड़ केरऽ वांगे कहैत छथि, “यदि क्वालीफाइंग चढ़ाई नेपाल धरि सीमित अछि त स्वाभाविक अछि जे पर्यटनक लाभ ओतहि रहैत अछि।” अतः ई नियम नेपाल केरऽ पहिने स॑ ही सुविकसित पर्वतारोहण अर्थव्यवस्था क॑ मजबूत करी सकै छै जबकि भारत म॑ तैयारी अभियान के आयोजन लेली प्रोत्साहन क॑ कमजोर करी सकै छै । जे पर्वतारोही अन्यथा भारतीय हिमालयी चोटी पर प्रशिक्षण ल सकैत छथि ओ निर्णय क सकैत छथि जे नेपाल मे पूरा प्रगति पूरा करब बेसी आर्थिक आ व्यावहारिक सार्थक अछि । वांगे न॑ कहलकै कि भारत केरऽ हिमालयी पर्वतारोहण अर्थव्यवस्था केरऽ सटीक मूल्य देना मुश्किल छै, लेकिन हुनी एकरा बहु अरब डॉलर केरऽ उद्योग बतैलकै जे देश भर म॑ सैकड़ों ट्रेकिंग आरू पर्वतारोहण क्लब क॑ समर्थन दै छै । हुनकऽ अनुमान छै कि अगर रिपोर्ट करलऽ गेलऽ क्वालीफायर क॑ लागू करलऽ जाय त॑ वू व्यवसाय के १५-२० प्रतिशत नेपाल म॑ शिफ्ट होय सकै छै । नेपाल मे 7000 मीटर के अनिवार्य तैयारी शिखर सम्मेलन मे सेहो आकांक्षी पर्वतारोही के चुटकी लेबय के संभावना अछि. फेडरल केरऽ बात करलऽ गेलऽ पर्वतारोही न॑ ई विषय प॑ नै उठैलकै, लेकिन रिपोर्टऽ स॑ पता चलै छै कि एवरेस्ट प॑ चढ़ै के अनुमति लेली ऐसनऽ मानदंड भारतीय पर्वतारोही सिनी के अभियान लागत म॑ कुछ लाख बढ़ाबै के तरह छै । वांगे के लेलऽ एकरऽ जवाब छै कि भारत तुलनीय भारतीय चढ़ाई के मान्यता लेली एगो मजबूत केस बनाबै । हुनकऽ मानना ​​छै कि भारत सरकार आरू भारतीय पर्वतारोहण फाउंडेशन क॑ नेपाल के साथ खास करी क॑ भारतीय पर्वतारोही के तरफ स॑ जुड़ना चाहियऽ । एकरऽ साथ ही हुनकऽ कहना छै कि ई बहस भारत क॑ अपनऽ कमी क॑ देखै लेली मजबूर करै के चाही । वांगे कहैत छथि जे एहि स भारत कए पर्वतारोहण मे बेसी गंभीरता स निवेश करबा लेल प्रोत्साहित करबाक चाही। स्वीकृत भारतीय चोटी क॑ मान्यता दै वाला बातचीत स॑ बनलऽ व्यवस्था भूगोल क॑ वैध अनुभव केरऽ एकमात्र मापदंड नै बनैने नेपाल केरऽ प्रस्ताव के पाछू के सुरक्षा सिद्धांत के सुरक्षा करी सकै छै । 1990 के दशक स॑ हिमालय म॑ सक्रिय रहलऽ दिग्गज पर्वतारोही कमल शर्मा के मानना ​​छै कि ई बहस ई भी दर्शाबै छै कि चढ़ाई के संस्कृति म॑ कतेक तेजी स॑ बदलाव आबी गेलऽ छै । ओ कहैत छथि जे पहिने चढ़ाई सालों क तैयारी क इनाम छल। “आइ शिखर पर पहुँचि कए देखाबय लेल बहुत बेसी दबाव अछि।” शर्मा एवरेस्ट स पहिने एकटा पूर्व शर्त क समर्थन करैत छथि मुदा आन लोक क तरह इ नहि मानैत छथि जे अनुभव तखने गिनल जेबाक चाही जखन ओ नेपाल मे भेटल। ओ कहैत छथि जे जौं कियो आन ठाम तुलनीय चोटी पर चढ़ि गेल अछि आ ओकरा साबित क सकैत अछि त ओहि मे सेहो गिनती हेबाक चाही। भारतीय पर्वतारोही सब सं गप्प-सप्पक पार एकटा बात पर व्यापक सहमति छल जे एवरेस्ट पर वास्तविक उच्च ऊँचाईक अनुभवक मांग करबाक चाही. असहमति तखने शुरू होइत अछि जखन भूगोल चर्चा मे प्रवेश करैत अछि ।

title: Nepal and Gavi Discuss Strategic Cooperation for 2027-2030 - Ratopati
description: Nepal and Gavi Discuss Strategic Cooperation for 2027-2030  Ratopati
publisher.title: Ratopati
full_article:
Kathmandu. High-level discussions were held between the Government of Nepal and 'Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance' on strategic cooperation from 2027 to 2030. In the meeting held between Health and Population Minister Nisha Mehta and a team led by Gavi's Senior Manager for Nepal, Nilgun Aydogan, discussions were held on vaccine cooperation for the next four years, co-financing, and financial sustainability of the program.

In the meeting, Gavi proposed to provide Nepal with vaccines worth 39.6 million US dollars and cash grants of 18.06 million US dollars for the upcoming period. Discussions were also held on the subject that Nepal would have to co-finance 17.1 million US dollars under the proposed assistance.

Cooperation between Nepal and Gavi began in 2001. In 25 years, Gavi has supported vaccines, cold chain infrastructure, and health system strengthening in Nepal worth more than 550 million US dollars, the Ministry of Health stated.

Currently, Gavi co-finances 5 out of the 11 vaccines provided by the Nepali government through the national immunization program, and provides one type of vaccine free of charge. Gavi's support has been ongoing in the operation of regular immunization as well as various vaccination campaigns through the National Immunization Program under the Family Welfare Division.

In the meeting, a thorough discussion was also held on how to make Nepal's national immunization program sustainable in the coming days amidst the global decline in development assistance and financial resources.

Gavi representatives praised the leadership shown by Minister Mehta in the national immunization program and the progress achieved by Nepal in the field of vaccination, and expressed their commitment to continue cooperation in the coming days.

वर्तमान मे गवी नेपाली सरकार द्वारा राष्ट्रीय टीकाकरण कार्यक्रम कें माध्यम सं उपलब्ध करायल गेल 11 टीका मे सं 5 टीकाक कें सह-वित्तपोषण करयत छै, आ एक प्रकार कें टीका निःशुल्क उपलब्ध करयत छै. परिवार कल्याण प्रभाग कें तहत राष्ट्रीय टीकाकरण कार्यक्रम कें माध्यम सं नियमित टीकाकरण कें संचालन कें साथ-साथ विभिन्न टीकाकरण अभियानक मे गैवी कें सहयोग जारी रहल छै.

बैसार मे विकास सहायता आ आर्थिक संसाधन मे वैश्विक गिरावट के बीच आगामी दिन मे नेपाल के राष्ट्रीय टीकाकरण कार्यक्रम के कोना टिकाऊ बनाओल जाय ताहि पर सेहो गहन चर्चा भेल।

title: India’s Communal Violence is Crossing into Nepal - The Diplomat – Asia-Pacific
description: India’s Communal Violence is Crossing into Nepal  The Diplomat – Asia-Pacific
publisher.title: The Diplomat – Asia-Pacific
full_article:
Nepal’s Tarai-Madhesh region abutting India appears increasingly prone to religious strife. With the sway of India’s Hindu nationalist groups like the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) steadily building on Nepali soil, the country is also witnessing more Hindu-Muslim tensions. While common in north India, such incidents had been rare in Nepal until recently.

Earlier this month, four Nepali youths were killed in clashes with police. The immediate cause of the incident was a Hindu procession passing through Dewanjung in Sunsari district, blasting loud music. The local Muslims protested. A clash ensued, police intervened and three youths were killed. (A fourth died in related protests in another district.) Local accounts suggest the Hindus in the area were already angry as the organizers of Muharram — a festival that marks the start of the Islamic calendar — had yet to remove some green pennants planted for the festival a month before.

According to one newspaper investigation, there were at least 17 such incidents of Hindu-Muslim tensions in the Tarai belt in the past eight years.

Earlier, Nepali Hindus seldom felt the need to publicly assert their religious identity. But as the Hindu forces in India started the rather brazen display of anti-Muslim activities starting in the early 1990s — most infamous of which was the 1992 demolition of the Babri Masjid in Ayodhya — the observation of Hindu festivals and rituals also began to change in Nepal.

By the time of the inauguration of the Ram Temple in India’s Ayodhya in January 2024, rooftop saffron flags had become a common sight in Hindu homes in the Tarai-Madhesh. As religious identities became more publicly politicized, saffron flags were increasingly answered by green pennants in Muslim households. Again emulating practices across the border, elaborate religious processions accompanied by loud music also became common among Nepali Hindus and Muslims alike.

The BJP’s rhetoric that all Muslims are basically anti-Hindu and must thus be resisted has also taken root thanks to the vocal advocacy of pro-Hindu, BJP-linked groups active in Nepal. They often cite reports of growing radicalization of madrassas in the region and entry of Rohingya refugees to justify their activism. The Indian security establishment under the BJP in particular has consistently pushed this line.

Nepal’s interim constitution promulgated in 2007 following the end of the Maoist insurgency had declared Nepal a secular state. Yet by 2015, the demand for a Hindu state had again started gaining traction. One reason for India’s imposition of a months-long blockade on Nepal at the time of the promulgation of the new constitution in 2015 was that the Nepali political class had ignored the BJP-led government’s wish that the new charter restore Nepal as a Hindu state.

Come 2026, the risk of the use of religion as a political tool is growing in Nepal. The country’s constitution bans the registration of political parties along religious lines. But if the polarization between Hindus on the one hand and Muslims (and even Christians) on the other keeps rising, major parties could face greater electoral pressure to more publicly embrace Hinduism: 81 percent of Nepalis are Hindu. There are already significant pro-Hindu state constituencies in all of Nepal’s major parties.

The 2015 constitution, while declaring that the country is a secular state, added the rider that secularism also means “protection of religion and culture handed down from time immemorial.” As the phrase is commonly understood to refer primarily to Hindu traditions, the provision gives the majority faith an implicit constitutional privilege.

This definition of secularism was a fudge to accommodate both pro-Hindu and secular constituencies. Yet such vagueness does not seem to be helping the cause of any community: A substantial share of Hindus want a de jure Hindu state; religious minorities, including Muslims who make up just over five percent of the population, feel more and more marginalized and want the Nepali state’s unconditional commitment to secularism.

The risk is that these sporadic clashes will become systemic and more difficult for Kathmandu to control. The Balendra Shah government’s handling of recent tensions left a lot to be desired. At the start, the incident in Sunsari was treated as a law and order problem and Nepal Police used disproportionate force to contain rioters—which paradoxically inflamed the whole region.

As communal tensions heightened across the Tarai-Madhesh belt, Prime Minister Shah refused to address the nation and appeal for calm. It was only when things threatened to spiral out of control that Shah finally addressed the country on the fifth day of the Sunsari police firing. Tensions began to die down the very next day.

But to maintain lasting religious harmony and preserve Nepal’s secular character, there must be broad political consensus in favor of separation of religion and politics. This can include an explicit commitment by political parties not to campaign on religious lines and greater representation of minorities in local administration and policing.

Unlike in India, Nepali political parties have a track record of setting aside their differences and uniting in the national interest during times of crisis. This time too all the major parties came together to appeal for communal harmony.

Yet when political competition becomes centered on faith, compromise becomes far harder. As India’s example suggests, parties can bargain over policies and power, but rarely over sacred identities.

भारत स॑ सटलऽ नेपाल केरऽ तराई-मधेश क्षेत्र म॑ धार्मिक कलह केरऽ प्रवृत्ति बढ़ी रहलऽ नजर आबी रहलऽ छै । भारत केरऽ राष्ट्रीय स्वयंसेवक संघ जैसनऽ भारत केरऽ हिन्दू राष्ट्रवादी समूह केरऽ दबदबा के साथ नेपाली धरती प॑ लगातार बढ़ी रहलऽ छै, ई देश म॑ भी हिन्दू-मुस्लिम केरऽ अधिक तनाव देखलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै । उत्तर भारत मे आम रहला पर नेपाल मे एहि तरहक घटना हाल धरि दुर्लभ छल ।

एहि मासक प्रारंभ मे पुलिस सं भेल झड़प मे चारिटा नेपाली युवक के मौत भ गेल छल. घटना के तत्काल कारण सुनसरी जिला के देवानजंग स गुजरैत हिन्दू जुलूस जोरदार संगीत के धमाका करैत छल। स्थानीय मुसलमान विरोध केलक। झड़प भेल, पुलिस हस्तक्षेप केलक आ तीन युवक के मौत भ गेल। (एकटा दोसर जिला में संबंधित विरोध प्रदर्शन में चारिम के मौत भ गेलैन।) स्थानीय विवरण सं पता चलैत अछि जे एहि इलाका के हिन्दू सब पहिने सं नाराज छलाह, कारण मुहर्रम - जे इस्लामी कैलेंडर के शुरुआत होइत अछि - के आयोजक सब के एखन धरि एक महीना पहिने एहि पावनि के लेल लगाओल गेल किछु हरियर पेनंट नहिं हटाबय के छल.

एक अखबार केरऽ जांच के अनुसार तराई बेल्ट म॑ पिछला आठ साल म॑ कम स॑ कम १७ ऐसनऽ घटना घटलऽ छै ।

पहिने नेपाली हिन्दू लोकनि केँ अपन धार्मिक पहिचान केँ सार्वजनिक रूप सँ पुष्ट करबाक आवश्यकता बहुत कम बुझाइत छलनि । लेकिन जेना-जेना भारत में हिन्दू सेना 1990 के दशक के शुरुआत में शुरू होय वाला मुस्लिम विरोधी गतिविधि के एकदम बेशर्म प्रदर्शन शुरू करलकै — जेकरा में सबसें कुख्यात छेलै 1992 में अयोध्या में बाबरी मस्जिद के तोड़ना — नेपाल में हिन्दू पर्व आरू संस्कार के पालन में भी बदलाव आबै लागलै ।

जनवरी २०२४ म॑ भारत केरऽ अयोध्या म॑ राम मंदिर केरऽ उद्घाटन के समय तलक तराई-मधेश केरऽ हिन्दू घरऽ म॑ छत प॑ केसर केरऽ झंडा आम दृश्य बनी गेलऽ छेलै । जेना-जेना धार्मिक पहचान के सार्वजनिक रूप स॑ राजनीतिकरण होय गेलै, मुस्लिम घरऽ म॑ केसर के झंडा के जवाब हरियर पेनंट स॑ मिलै लगलै । पुनः सीमा पारक प्रथाक अनुकरण करैत जोर-जोर सँ संगीतक संग विस्तृत धार्मिक जुलूस सेहो नेपाली हिन्दू आ मुसलमान मे आम भ गेल ।

भाजपा केरऽ ई बयानबाजी कि सब मुसलमान मूल रूप स॑ हिन्दू विरोधी छै आरू ई तरह स॑ एकरऽ विरोध करना जरूरी छै, ई भी नेपाल म॑ सक्रिय हिन्दू समर्थक, भाजपा स॑ जुड़लऽ समूहऽ के मुखर वकालत के बदौलत जड़ जमाय लेल॑ छै । हुनी अक्सर अपनऽ सक्रियता क॑ जायज ठहराबै लेली ई क्षेत्र म॑ मदरसा केरऽ बढ़तऽ कट्टरता आरू रोहिंग्या शरणार्थी केरऽ प्रवेश के खबर के हवाला दै छै । खास क भाजपा क तहत भारतीय सुरक्षा प्रतिष्ठान लगातार एहि रेखा कए आगू बढ़बैत रहल अछि।

माओवादी विद्रोह समाप्त भेलाक बाद २००७ मे जारी नेपालक अन्तरिम संविधान मे नेपाल केँ धर्मनिरपेक्ष राज्य घोषित कएने छल । तइयो 2015 तक हिन्दू राज्य क मांग कए फेर स कर्षण भेटब शुरू भ गेल छल। 2015 मे नव संविधान जारी हेबाक समय भारत द्वारा नेपाल पर महीनो धरि नाकाबंदी करबाक एकटा कारण ईहो छल जे नेपाली राजनीतिक वर्ग भाजपा नेतृत्वक सरकारक इच्छा केँ अनदेखी कएने छल जे नव चार्टर मे नेपाल केँ हिन्दू राज्यक रूप मे बहाल कयल जाय।

आऊ 2026 नेपाल मे धर्म के राजनीतिक औजार के रूप में प्रयोग के जोखिम बढ़ि रहल अछि। देश के संविधान मे धार्मिक तर्ज पर राजनीतिक दल के पंजीकरण पर रोक लगा देल गेल अछि. लेकिन अगर एक तरफ हिन्दू आरू दोसरऽ तरफ मुसलमान (आरू ईसाई भी) के बीच ध्रुवीकरण बढ़त॑ रहतै त॑ बड़ऽ दलऽ प॑ हिन्दू धर्म क॑ अधिक सार्वजनिक रूप स॑ अपनाबै लेली चुनावी दबाव के सामना करना पड़॑ सकै छै : ८१ प्रतिशत नेपाली हिन्दू छै । नेपाल केरऽ सब प्रमुख दल म॑ पहल॑ स॑ ही महत्वपूर्ण हिन्दू समर्थक राज्य निर्वाचन क्षेत्र छै ।

2015 केरऽ संविधान म॑ देश क॑ धर्मनिरपेक्ष राज्य के घोषणा करतें हुअ॑ सवार क॑ जोड़लऽ गेलै कि धर्मनिरपेक्षता केरऽ मतलब भी छै “अनादि काल स॑ चलै वाला धर्म आरू संस्कृति केरऽ सुरक्षा” । जेना कि ई वाक्यांश क॑ आम तौर प॑ मुख्य रूप स॑ हिन्दू परंपरा के संदर्भ म॑ समझलऽ जाय छै, ई प्रावधान स॑ बहुसंख्यक आस्था क॑ एक अन्तर्निहित संवैधानिक विशेषाधिकार मिलै छै ।

धर्मनिरपेक्षता के ई परिभाषा हिन्दू समर्थक आ धर्मनिरपेक्ष दुनू क्षेत्र के समायोजित करय के फज छल. तइयो एहन अस्पष्टता कोनो समुदायक काजमें सहायक नहिं बुझाइत अछि : हिन्दूक पर्याप्त हिस्सा डी जूरे हिन्दू राज्य चाहैत अछि ; धार्मिक अल्पसंख्यक, जेकरा म॑ मुसलमान भी शामिल छै, जे आबादी केरऽ पांच प्रतिशत स॑ कुछ अधिक छै, अधिक स॑ अधिक हाशिया प॑ महसूस करै छै आरू नेपाली राज्य केरऽ धर्मनिरपेक्षता के प्रति बिना शर्त प्रतिबद्धता चाहै छै ।

जोखिम ई छै कि ई छिटपुट झड़प प्रणालीगत होय जैतै आरू काठमांडू लेली नियंत्रण करना मुश्किल होय जैतै । हाल के तनाव के निपटारा बलेन्द्र शाह सरकार के तरफ सं बहुत किछ छोड़ि देल गेल. शुरू में सुनसरी के घटना के कानून व्यवस्था के समस्या के रूप में देखल गेल आ नेपाल पुलिस दंगाई के रोकय लेल असमान बल के प्रयोग केलक-जे विरोधाभासी रूप स पूरा क्षेत्र के भड़का देलक।

तराई-मधेश पट्टी भरि साम्प्रदायिक तनाव बढ़ला पर प्रधानमंत्री शाह राष्ट्र के संबोधित करय आ शांति के अपील करय सं मना क देलखिन्ह. जखन बात बेकाबू होबय के खतरा छल तखनहि शाह आखिरकार सुनसरी पुलिस के गोलीबारी के पांचम दिन देश के संबोधित केलखिन्ह. तनाव ठीक दोसर दिन मरि जाय लागल।

लेकिन स्थायी धार्मिक सौहार्द कायम रखै लेली आरू नेपाल केरऽ धर्मनिरपेक्ष चरित्र क॑ बचाबै लेली धर्म आरू राजनीति केरऽ पृथक्करण के पक्ष म॑ व्यापक राजनीतिक सहमति होना जरूरी छै । एहि मे राजनीतिक दल द्वारा धार्मिक लाइन पर प्रचार नहि करबाक स्पष्ट प्रतिबद्धता आ स्थानीय प्रशासन आ पुलिसिंग मे अल्पसंख्यकक बेसी प्रतिनिधित्व शामिल भ सकैत अछि ।

भारत के विपरीत नेपाली राजनीतिक दल के संकट के समय में अपन मतभेद के एक कात राखि राष्ट्रीय हित में एकजुट होय के ट्रैक रिकॉर्ड अछि. एहि बेर सेहो सब पैघ दल एक संग आबि साम्प्रदायिक सौहार्द क अपील केलक।

तइयो जखन राजनीतिक प्रतिस्पर्धा आस्था पर केंद्रित भ' जाइत अछि त' समझौता कहीं कठिन भ' जाइत अछि. जेना कि भारत केरऽ उदाहरण स॑ पता चलै छै कि पार्टी नीति आरू सत्ता प॑ मोलभाव करी सकै छै, लेकिन पवित्र पहचान प॑ शायद ही कभी ।

description: Nepal pitches itself as India-China bridge amid balanced diplomacy  India Today
publisher.title: India Today
full_article:
Nepal wants to transform itself from a landlocked country into a "vibrant, dynamic bridge" connecting India and China, Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal said on Friday, underlining Kathmandu's effort to maintain balanced ties with its two neighbours.

Speaking at the inauguration of a two-day international conference titled 'China and South Asia in a Multipolar World', Khanal said Nepal welcomed the continued development and prosperity of both India and China. He said the country remained committed to strengthening relations with both on the basis of "sovereign equality, mutual respect, mutual benefit, and sensitivity to each other's legitimate interests and concerns".

The conference was jointly organised by the Centre for South Asian Studies, Fudan University, China, and the Nepal Institute for International Cooperation and Engagement.

Khanal's remarks are significant as Nepal's new government led by Prime Minister Balendra Shah has sought to pursue a balanced foreign policy towards its two immediate neighbours, while placing greater emphasis on economic diplomacy, investment and connectivity.

"Asia's transformation presents unprecedented opportunities for shared prosperity," Khanal said, adding that South Asia has enormous promise even though much of its economic potential remains untapped.

He said economic diplomacy had become "one of the defining priorities" of Nepal's external engagement and that the country's foreign policy was aimed at improving the lives of its people through trade, investment, employment, tourism, technology, innovation and sustainable development.

"Nepal sincerely welcomes the continued development and prosperity of both India and China and remains committed to further strengthening its longstanding bilateral relations with both neighbours independently, on the basis of sovereign equality, mutual respect, mutual benefit, and sensitivity to each other's legitimate interests and concerns," he said.

"Nepal aspires to transform itself from a landlocked country into a vibrant, dynamic bridge connecting China and India," Khanal added.

Khanal's back-to-back visits to New Delhi and Beijing in June were seen as an early indication of Kathmandu's effort to maintain balanced ties with both neighbours. He had earlier said Nepal wanted to build stronger and deeper relations with both India and China, describing its southern and northern neighbours as vital partners for the Himalayan nation. Overall, his remarks on Friday reinforced Nepal's push to deepen ties with both countries while focusing on economic diplomacy and connectivity.

‘बहुध्रुवीय विश्व मे चीन आ दक्षिण एशिया’ नामक दू दिवसीय अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय सम्मेलनक उद्घाटन मे खनाल भारत आ चीन दुनूक निरंतर विकास आ समृद्धिके नेपाल स्वागत करैत बतौलनि । हुनी कहलकै कि देश “सार्वभौमिक समानता, आपसी सम्मान, आपसी लाभ, आरू एक-दूसरा के जायज हित आरू सरोकार के प्रति संवेदनशीलता” के आधार प दोनों के साथ संबंध मजबूत करै लेली प्रतिबद्ध छै ।

description: Chilling discovery as snow melts away in Nepal’s Rolwaling Valley  independent.co.uk
publisher.title: independent.co.uk
full_article:
Human remains, believed to be five climbers missing since an avalanche last November, have been located in Nepal's Rolwaling Valley.

The bodies were exposed at Yalung Ri base camp this week as seasonal snow melted, nearly nine months after the disaster.

Local residents reported the discovery on Thursday, prompting a police team to attempt recovery on Friday.

Poor weather conditions prevented the immediate retrieval of the remains, which are yet to be formally identified.

The five are thought to be among seven climbers, including foreign nationals and Nepali guides, who were swept away in the 3 November avalanche, with two bodies recovered shortly after.

title: Nepal’s demolition drive leaves thousands homeless, violates human rights - Scroll.in
description: Nepal’s demolition drive leaves thousands homeless, violates human rights  Scroll.in
publisher.title: Scroll.in
full_article:
The mass eviction of slums and informal settlements in Nepal’s capital Kathmandu and surrounding districts has displaced an estimated 15,000-20,000 people.

On April 25, the Nepal government began forcibly removing landless residents from the Kathmandu Valley, later extending the drive beyond the capital.

Nepal faces a staggering crisis: more than 3.5 million people are landless or homeless. A government commission invited applications for registration, and 1.2 million people – mostly poor, Dalit, and indigenous – have already registered in the hope of receiving land. Ironically, these communities have borne the brunt of evictions carried out without adequate notice, consultation, or alternative housing. The lack of support has eroded their trust in the state.

The ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party pledged to resolve landlessness within 1,000 days of office. Its 100-point action plan also promised relief to the landless. Yet, despite decades of settlement – some families have been living in Kathmandu’s slums for 60 years – the government demolished homes using the full force of the state. Nepal Police, Armed Police Force, Nepal Army, and the municipal police participated. Residents were harassed, threatened, and even detained before demolitions.

Authorities report 2,687 houses destroyed, affecting 15,300 people since April 25. District Administration Office data show 2,501 families – 15,316 people, including 3,133 schoolchildren – evicted between April 25 and May 4, this year.

Eviction notices were issued on April 22, with demolitions beginning early on April 25. Most residents were daily wage labourers, sanitation workers, shopkeepers, or informal sector employees. As bulldozers rolled in, women and children cried while men were away at work. Security forces cordoned off areas, barring civil society observers.

Evicted families were taken to the Rangashala (City Stadium) for verification. A High-Powered Committee for Integrated Development of Bagmati Civilization was tasked with verifying landless residents along the Bagmati riverbank. The government required that the evicted register for support.

However, families – busy salvaging belongings – could not comply. Confusion surrounding the eviction and the resulting insecurity compounded the problem. As the security forces cordoned off the area, human rights defenders and journalists were denied access, rendering the process humiliating and opaque.

Seven holding centres were established in Kathmandu, Bhaktapur, and Kavre. These centres were heavily securitised, forbade movement outside the centres and subjected the residents to harassment. Though the government promised food and durable solutions, security personnel pressured families to leave. Nepal’s National Human Rights Commission reported ultimatums requiring displaced people to vacate centres, threats, and conditions leading to food insecurity.

Children suffered acutely. Many were scheduled to sit for 2026/27 school exams on April 16, and faced disruption because of the evictions. As families were scattered, not only was children’s education interrupted, they also endured discrimination and humiliation amongst their peers. As 63 percent of slum residents are estimated to be women, young mothers faced added burdens of childcare, insecurity, and humiliation.

Eventually, the government stopped food and water supplies in holding centres and chose to offer Nepali rupees 25,000 (about US $162) as compensation to the evicted families. They were urged to seek rented accommodation. This token support, coupled with forced removal from centres, underscored official impunity. Clearly, the authorities demolished the slums without assuming responsibility for consequences.

The evictions were criticised and condemned by international and national organisations. They urged immediate suspension of the drive and reminded the Nepal government that it should follow national laws and the Guiding Principles on Internal Displacement. They mandate eviction notices to be issued in advance, consultation with the target communities, data recording, and the provision of alternative housing.

Instead, the official chose the path of systematic repression. Already living on the margins, surveillance and securitised centres marginalised the evicted people further. Security forces pressured families to accept NPR 25,000 and leave, revealing the absence of a resettlement plan.

The haphazard evictions undermined rights guaranteed by Nepal’s 2015 Constitution. These included Article 27 – Right to Information; Article 35 – Right to Health; Article 36 – Right to Food; and Article 37 – Right to Housing.

Thus several fundamental human rights were violated.

On April 23, a writ petition was filed in the Supreme Court seeking to halt demolitions until alternative housing was provided. The Court delayed issuing a show-cause order but, on May 8, finally granted an interim order stopping evictions. It expressed concern over holding centre mismanagement and deprivation of shelter, education, healthcare, and housing. The Court directed the government not to resume evictions and to provide effective services, while insisting that prescribed legal procedures be followed in future.

Nepal urgently needs a comprehensive, sustainable solution. This would entail consultation with affected communities, ensuring legal compliance with eviction procedures, and involving local government bodies in registering landless families, screening communities, and identifying land for resettlement.

Without such measures, forced mass displacement will remain a grave human rights violation, deepen vulnerability and erode constitutional guarantees.

Som Niroula is a research scholar at the Department of Conflict, Peace and Development, Tribhuvan University, Kathmandu, Nepal. He is also a member of the CRG Research Collective, Calcutta, and was a Junior Fellow at Institut für die Wissenschaften vom Menschen, Vienna.

नेपाल के राजधानी काठमांडू आ आसपास के जिला में झुग्गी-झोपड़ी आ अनौपचारिक बस्ती के सामूहिक बेदखली के कारण अनुमानित 15-20 हजार लोक विस्थापित भ गेल अछि.

25 अप्रैल कए नेपाल सरकार काठमांडू घाटी स भूमिहीन निवासी कए जबरदस्ती हटाबय लागल, बाद मे एहि अभियान कए राजधानी स आगू बढ़ा देलक।

नेपाल मे एकटा डगमगाइत संकट अछि : 35 लाख सँ बेसी लोक भूमिहीन वा बेघर छथि । एकटा सरकारी आयोग पंजीकरणक लेल आवेदन आमंत्रित केलक, आ 12 लाख लोक – जाहि मे बेसीतर गरीब, दलित, आ मूल निवासी – जमीन भेटबाक आशा मे पंजीकरण करा चुकल छथि। विडंबना ई छै कि ई समुदायऽ न॑ बिना पर्याप्त सूचना, परामर्श, या वैकल्पिक आवास के करलऽ गेलऽ बेदखली के बोझ उठाय लेल॑ छै । समर्थन के कमी के कारण राज्य पर हुनकर विश्वास खत्म भ गेल अछि.

सत्तारूढ़ राष्ट्रिय स्वतंत्र पार्टी कार्यकाल के एक हजार दिन के भीतर भूमिहीनता के समाधान करय के वचन देलक अछि। एकर 100 सूत्री कार्य योजना मे भूमिहीन कए राहत देबाक वादा सेहो कैल गेल छल। तइयो दशकों बस्ती के बादो – किछु परिवार 60 साल स काठमांडू के झुग्गी-झोपड़ी मे रहैत अछि – सरकार राज्य के पूर्ण बल के प्रयोग क घर तोड़ि देलक। नेपाल प्रहरी, सशस्त्र प्रहरी बल, नेपाल सेना, आ नगर प्रहरी सहभागिता रहल अछि । निवासी सब के परेशान करलऽ गेलै, धमकी देलऽ गेलै, आरू तोड़ै स॑ पहल॑ भी हिरासत म॑ लेलऽ गेलै ।

अधिकारि सब के रिपोर्ट अछि जे 25 अप्रैल सं 2,687 घर नष्ट भ गेल अछि, जाहि सं 15,300 लोक प्रभावित भ गेल अछि.जिला प्रशासन कार्यालय के आंकड़ा बता रहल अछि जे एहि साल 25 अप्रैल सं 4 मई के बीच 2,501 परिवार – 15,316 लोक, जाहि मे 3,133 स्कूली बच्चा सेहो शामिल अछि – बेदखल भ गेल अछि.

22 अप्रैल कए बेदखली क नोटिस जारी कैल गेल छल, जाहि मे 25 अप्रैल स जल्दी तोड़बाक काज शुरू भ गेल छल।अधिकांश निवासी दैनिक मजदूर, स्वच्छता मजदूर, दुकानदार, या अनौपचारिक क्षेत्र क कर्मचारी छलाह। बुलडोजर घुमैत-फिरैत महिला आ बच्चा सब कानय लागल जखन कि पुरुष काज पर दूर छल। सुरक्षा बल नागरिक समाज के पर्यवेक्षक के छोड़ि क इलाका के घेराबंदी केलक।

बेदखल परिवार के सत्यापन के लेल रंगशाला (सिटी स्टेडियम) ल गेल गेल। बागमती सभ्यता के एकीकृत विकास के लेल एकटा उच्च शक्ति वाला समिति के बागमती नदी के किनारे भूमिहीन निवासी के सत्यापन के जिम्मा देल गेल छल. सरकार के तरफ सं बेदखल लोक के समर्थन के लेल रजिस्टर करय के जरूरत छल.

मुदा, परिवार – सामान बचाबय मे व्यस्त – एकर पालन नहि क’ सकल. बेदखली के ल क भ्रम आ परिणामस्वरूप असुरक्षा समस्या के और बढ़ा देलक। जेना-जेना सुरक्षा बल एहि इलाका कए घेराबंदी केलक, मानव अधिकार रक्षक आ पत्रकार कए प्रवेश स मना क देल गेल, जाहि स इ प्रक्रिया अपमानजनक आ अपारदर्शी भ गेल।

काठमांडू, भक्तपुर, आ काभ्रे मे सातटा होल्डिंग सेंटर स्थापित भेल । एहि केंद्र सब पर भारी सुरक्षा छल, केंद्र स बाहर आवागमन पर रोक लगा देल गेल आ निवासी कए उत्पीड़न क शिकार बनाउल गेल। सरकार भले ही भोजन आरू टिकाऊ समाधान के वादा करलकै, लेकिन सुरक्षाकर्मी परिवारऽ प॑ दबाव डाललकै कि वू बाहर निकली जाय । नेपाल केरऽ राष्ट्रीय मानवाधिकार आयोग न॑ अल्टीमेटम के रिपोर्ट देल॑ छै कि विस्थापित लोगऽ क॑ केंद्र खाली करै के जरूरत छै, खतरा, आरू खाद्य असुरक्षा पैदा करै वाला परिस्थिति ।

बच्चा सब के तीव्र कष्ट भेल। बहुतो के 16 अप्रैल के 2026/27 के स्कूल परीक्षा में बैसय के छल, आओर बेदखली के कारण बाधा के सामना करय पड़ल. जेना-जेना परिवार छिड़ियाइत गेल, बच्चा सभक पढ़ाई मे बाधा त’ भेलै, संगहि ओ सभ अपन साथी सभक बीच भेदभाव आ अपमान सेहो सहैत रहल. जेना कि झुग्गी-झोपड़ी मे 63 प्रतिशत निवासी महिला हेबाक अनुमान अछि, युवा मां कए बच्चा क देखभाल, असुरक्षा, आ अपमान क अतिरिक्त बोझ क सामना करय पड़ल।

अन्ततः सरकार होल्डिंग सेंटर मे भोजन आ जल आपूर्ति बंद क देलक आ बेदखल परिवार कए मुआवजा क रूप मे नेपाली टका 25 हजार (लगभग 162 अमेरिकी डॉलर) देब पसिन केलक। किराया पर आवास तकबाक आग्रह कएल गेल। ई टोकन समर्थन के साथ-साथ केंद्रऽ स॑ जबरन हटाबै के काम आधिकारिक दंडहीनता प॑ जोर देलकै । स्पष्ट अछि जे अधिकारी बिना परिणाम क जिम्मेदारी लेने झुग्गी-झोपड़ी कए तोड़ि देलक।

एहि बेदखली क आलोचना आ निंदा अंतरराष्ट्रीय आ राष्ट्रीय संगठन सब केलक। ओ सब अभियान के तत्काल निलंबन करबाक आग्रह करैत नेपाल सरकार के राष्ट्रीय कानून आ आन्तरिक विस्थापन के मार्गदर्शक सिद्धांत के पालन करबाक चाही से मोन पाड़लनि। ओ बेदखली कें सूचना पहिने सं जारी करनाय, लक्षित समुदायक सं परामर्श, डाटा रिकॉर्डिंग, आ वैकल्पिक आवास कें प्रावधान कें अनिवार्य करय छै.

बल्कि अधिकारी व्यवस्थित दमनक बाट चुनलनि। पहिने स हाशिया पर रहैत निगरानी आ प्रतिभूतिकृत केंद्र बेदखल लोक कए आओर हाशिया पर राखि देलक। सुरक्षा बल परिवार सब पर एनपीआर 25 हजार स्वीकार करय आ ओतय सं चलि जेबाक दबाव बनौलक, जाहि सं पुनर्वास योजना के अभाव के खुलासा भेल.

बेतरतीब बेदखली स नेपाल के 2015 के संविधान के गारंटी वाला अधिकार के नुकसान पहुंचल. एहि मे अनुच्छेद 27 – सूचनाक अधिकार; अनुच्छेद ३५ – स्वास्थ्यक अधिकार; अनुच्छेद ३६ – भोजनक अधिकार; आ अनुच्छेद 37 – आवासक अधिकार।

एहि तरहें कतेको मौलिक मानव अधिकारक उल्लंघन भेल ।

23 अप्रैल कए सुप्रीम कोर्ट मे रिट याचिका दायर कैल गेल जे जा धरि वैकल्पिक आवास क व्यवस्था नहि भ जाएत ता धरि तोड़फोड़ कए रोकल जाए। कोर्ट कारण देखाबय के आदेश जारी करय मे देरी केलक मुदा 8 मई के आखिरकार बेदखली रोकय के अंतरिम आदेश देलक. एहि मे केंद्र क कुप्रबंधन आ आवास, शिक्षा, स्वास्थ्य सेवा, आ आवास स वंचित रहबा पर चिंता व्यक्त कैल गेल। कोर्ट न॑ सरकार क॑ निर्देश देलकै कि बेदखली क॑ दोबारा नै शुरू करलऽ जाय आरू प्रभावी सेवा देलऽ जाय, जबकि भविष्य म॑ निर्धारित कानूनी प्रक्रिया के पालन करै के जिद करलऽ गेलै ।

नेपाल के एकटा व्यापक, टिकाऊ समाधान के तत्काल आवश्यकता अछि। अइ मे प्रभावित समुदायक सं परामर्श, बेदखली प्रक्रियाक कें कानूनी अनुपालन सुनिश्चित करनाय, आ स्थानीय सरकारी निकाय कें भूमिहीन परिवारक कें पंजीकरण, समुदायक कें जांच, आ पुनर्वास कें लेल जमीन कें पहचान करनाय मे शामिल करनाय आवश्यक होयत.

एहन उपाय के बिना जबरदस्ती सामूहिक विस्थापन मानव अधिकार के गंभीर उल्लंघन बनल रहत, कमजोरी के गहींर करत आ संवैधानिक गारंटी के क्षरण करत।

सोम निरौला नेपाल के काठमांडू स्थित त्रिभुवन विश्वविद्यालय के द्वंद्व, शान्ति एवं विकास विभाग में शोध विद्वान हैं | ओ सीआरजी रिसर्च कलेक्टिव, कलकत्ता के सदस्य सेहो छैथ, आ वियना के इंस्टीट्यूट फर डाई विसेनशाफ्टन वोम मेनशेन में जूनियर फेलो छलाह.

title: Nepal Eyes Strategic Role as Bridge Between India and China - Deccan Chronicle
description: Nepal Eyes Strategic Role as Bridge Between India and China  Deccan Chronicle
publisher.title: Deccan Chronicle
full_article:
Kathmandu: Nepal wants to transform itself from a landlocked country into a "vibrant, dynamic bridge" connecting India and China, Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal said here on Friday.

Nepal welcomed the continued development and prosperity of both India and China, Khanal said as he inaugurated a two-day international conference titled 'China and South Asia in a Multipolar World.'

The foreign minister added that Nepal remained committed to strengthening its relations with both its neighbours based on "sovereign equality, mutual respect, mutual benefit, and sensitivity to each other's legitimate interests and concerns."

The conference was jointly organised by the Centre for South Asian Studies, Fudan University, China, and Nepal Institute for International Cooperation and Engagement.

The remarks assume significance as Nepal's new government led by Prime Minister Balendra Shah has sought to pursue a balanced foreign policy towards its two immediate neighbours while placing greater emphasis on economic diplomacy, investment and connectivity.

"Asia's transformation presents unprecedented opportunities for shared prosperity," Khanal said, stressing that South Asia possesses enormous promise, although much of its economic potential remains untapped.

He said economic diplomacy had become "one of the defining priorities" of Nepal's external engagement and that the country's foreign policy was aimed at improving the lives of its people through trade, investment, employment, tourism, technology, innovation and sustainable development.

"Nepal sincerely welcomes the continued development and prosperity of both India and China and remains committed to further strengthening its longstanding bilateral relations with both neighbours independently, on the basis of sovereign equality, mutual respect, mutual benefit, and sensitivity to each other's legitimate interests and concerns," he said.

"Nepal aspires to transform itself from a landlocked country into a vibrant, dynamic bridge connecting China and India," Khanal added.

Khanal's back-to-back visits to New Delhi and Beijing in June were seen as an early indication of Kathmandu's effort to maintain balanced ties with both neighbours.

He had earlier said Nepal wants to build stronger and deeper relations with both India and China, describing the southern and northern neighbours as vital partners for the Himalayan nation.

full_article:
KATHMANDU: The 11th meeting of the Nepal Quality Council has approved draft Nepal Quality and International Standards aimed at improving quality regulation and aligning domestic practices with global standards.

The meeting endorsed various quality standards recommended by the technical committee formed for the determination and review of quality standards in Nepal.

Representatives from concerned ministries and officials from relevant organisations participated in the meeting.

The council approved specifications for ethanol used as a blending component in motor gasoline and standards related to elastomeric bridge bearings.

It also endorsed several international standards related to rubber hardness testing, along with standards for determining the compression set of rubber and thermoplastics.

According to the council, the decision was taken to update Nepal’s quality standards in line with current requirements and international practices.

The newly approved standards are expected to enhance quality in industrial and production sectors, strengthen testing systems and help Nepali products meet international benchmarks.

The council said the process of quality determination and review would also become more systematic and effective following the implementation of the updated standards.

title: Turmeric farming offers hope of reviving local employment in Nepal village - The Climate Watch
description: Turmeric farming offers hope of reviving local employment in Nepal village  The Climate Watch
publisher.title: The Climate Watch
full_article:
A community-led agroforestry initiative in Dhanusha is expanding income opportunities through turmeric cultivation, supported by FAO, while creating seasonal jobs and offering an alternative to overseas labour migration.

With their husbands working abroad, many women in Pushpalpur, Ward No. 4 of Mithila Municipality in Dhanusha district, Nepal, shoulder the responsibility of supporting their families on their own. While overseas employment has long been a necessity to sustain household incomes, these women are now beginning to see opportunities for earning a living within their own village. Turmeric cultivation, launched in the Bhatighari Community Forest, has become more than just an agricultural venture; it has given them renewed hope of reuniting their families by creating employment at home.

Meena Tamang, a resident of Pushpalpur, Ward No. 4, Mithila Municipality, says her husband is currently working overseas. Living apart from her family was never her choice but a necessity.

“My husband had to go abroad to support our family,” she says. “If we had a steady source of income here, I would want him to stay and work in the village instead.”

Most households in Pushpalpur have at least one male family member employed overseas. Buddhamaya Moktan, another resident of the village, also has a husband working abroad. Living with her two sons and one daughter, she dreams of having her family together again. For families forced to live apart due to the lack of local employment, the nearby Bhatighari Community Forest has become a source of hope.

The women believe that turmeric cultivation in the community forest will create employment opportunities in the coming years, allowing their husbands to return from overseas and find work in their own village. This year alone, they planted 5,400 kilograms of turmeric seed rhizomes in the community forest. According to Shyam Gole, chairperson of the Community Forest User Group, one quintal of turmeric seed can produce five to seven quintals of fresh turmeric. Based on this estimate, the group expects the 5,400 kg planted this year to yield approximately 32,400 kg of turmeric.

According to Meena Tamang, secretary of the Community Forest User Group, local people will be employed in activities such as cultivation, processing, packaging and marketing of turmeric.

“We plan to package and market the turmeric ourselves. Once that happens, many more people in the village will have employment opportunities,” she says.

In the Nepali market, ground turmeric powder currently sells for NPR 300 to NPR 600 per kilogram. Local initiatives have been supported by the Forest and Agriculture Facilitation Programme, implemented with assistance from the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO). Through the programme, the community has received turmeric seed, agricultural tools for land preparation and support for the construction of a turmeric processing centre.

A model community forest

Located about one kilometre from the East-West Mahendra Highway, the Bhatighari Community Forest has been successfully protected and managed through the active participation of residents. It has also emerged as an exemplary model of agroforestry.

The forest is home to more than 500 mango trees. Every year, once the trees begin flowering, the Community Forest User Group sells the standing mango crop to traders through advance contracts worth NPR 1 million to NPR 1.5 million.

Beyond generating income from mango production, the forest also creates employment for local people. Villagers are hired to clear undergrowth, maintain the forest and cultivate turmeric. Around 40 households receive employment for approximately 30 days each year, earning NPR 700 per day, providing an important source of seasonal income for the community.

मिथिला नगरपालिका वार्ड नम्बर ४ पुष्पलपुर निवासी मीना तामांग कहैत छथि जे हुनकर पति एखन विदेश मे काज क रहल छथि। परिवार स अलग रहब कहियो हुनकर पसंद नहि छल बल्कि एकटा आवश्यकता छल।

ओ कहैत छथि जे हमर पति कए हमर परिवार क भरण-पोषण लेल विदेश जेबाक छल। “जँ हमरा सभक एतय आमदनीक स्थिर स्रोत रहैत त’ हम चाहब जे ओ गाम मे रहि क’ ओकर बदला मे काज करथि।”

पुष्पलपुर मे अधिकांश घर मे कम स कम एकटा पुरुष परिवार क सदस्य विदेश मे काज करैत छथि। गामक एकटा आओर निवासी बुद्धमाया मोक्तान के सेहो पति विदेश मे काज करय वाला छथिन्ह. अपन दुनू बेटा आ एकटा बेटीक संग रहैत ओ सपना देखैत छथि जे फेर अपन परिवार एक संग रहब। स्थानीय रोजगार के अभाव में अलग-अलग रहय लेल मजबूर परिवार के लेल पास के भटिघारी सामुदायिक वन आशा के विषय बनि गेल अछि.

महिला सब के मानना ​​छै कि सामुदायिक जंगल में हल्दी के खेती स॑ आबै वाला सालऽ म॑ रोजगार के अवसर पैदा होतै, जेकरा स॑ हुनकऽ पति विदेश स॑ वापस आबी क॑ अपनऽ ही गाँव म॑ काम खोजै के मौका मिलतै । असगर एहि साल सामुदायिक जंगल मे 5400 किलो हल्दी बीज क प्रकंद रोपलथि। सामुदायिक वन उपयोगकर्ता समूह के अध्यक्ष श्याम गोले के अनुसार एक क्विंटल हल्दी के बीज स पांच स सात क्विंटल ताजा हल्दी के उत्पादन भ सकैत अछि। एहि अनुमान क आधार पर समूह कए उम्मीद अछि जे एहि साल रोपल गेल 5,400 किलोग्राम मे लगभग 32,400 किलो हल्दी क पैदावार होएत।

सामुदायिक वन उपयोगकर्ता समूह क सचिव मीना तामांग क अनुसार स्थानीय लोक कए हल्दी क खेती, प्रसंस्करण, पैकेजिंग आ विपणन जेहन गतिविधि मे नियुक्त कैल जाएत।

ओ कहैत छथि जे हम सब खुद हल्दी कए पैकेजिंग आ मार्केटिंग करबाक योजना बना रहल छी, एक बेर एहन भ गेल त गाम मे आओर कतेको लोक कए रोजगार क अवसर भेटत।

नेपाली बाजार मे पिसल हल्दी पाउडर एखन 300 स 600 एनपीआर प्रति किलो मे बिकाइत अछि। स्थानीय पहलक कें वन आ कृषि सुविधा कार्यक्रम कें समर्थन कैल गेल छै, जे संयुक्त राष्ट्र कें खाद्य आ कृषि संगठन (एफएओ) कें सहायता सं लागू कैल गेल छै. कार्यक्रम के माध्यम स समुदाय के हल्दी के बीज, जमीन तैयार करय लेल कृषि उपकरण आ हल्दी प्रसंस्करण केंद्र के निर्माण के लेल सहयोग भेटल अछि।

एकटा आदर्श सामुदायिक जंगल

एहि जंगल मे 500 स बेसी आमक गाछ अछि। हर साल एक बेर गाछक कें फूल शुरू भ गेलाक कें बाद सामुदायिक वन उपयोगकर्ता समूह 10 लाख सं 15 लाख एनपीआर कें अग्रिम अनुबंध कें माध्यम सं व्यापारियक कें खड़ा आम कें फसल बेचयत छै.
